(a) The mayor, or his designee, has the authority to suspend a license for a short-term period not to exceed ten days. The mayor's decision shall be in writing, with the term of the suspension and the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee. (Ord. No. 2000-6, § 1, 1-1-2001)
283:
(a) Except as provided in sections 6-187 and 6-188 no license which has been issued or which may hereafter be issued pursuant to this chapter shall be suspended or revoked, except for due cause as hereinafter defined, and after a hearing and upon the prior three-day written notice to the holder of the license of the time, place and purpose of the hearing and a statement of the charges upon which the hearing shall be held.
(b) "Due cause" for the suspension or revocation or such license shall consist of the violation of any federal or state law, administrative regulation or city ordinances regulating such business (including but not limited to any violation of this chapter), or the violation of any federal or state law, state administrative regulation or city ordinance prohibiting gambling, or regulating the sale, manufacture, distribution, handling, dealing in, and possession of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to underage persons in any unlawful manner, or the violation of any federal or state law, state administrative regulation or city ordinance relating to the manufacture, sale or distribution of any controlled substance.
(c) The hearing will be conducted by the mayor and council or by a hearing officer appointed by the mayor. The hearing officer shall be an attorney licensed to practice in the state.
(d) At the hearing the licensee shall have the right to represent itself or be represented by counsel, may cross-examine all witnesses offered by the city, and may present evidence in its own behalf. Formal rules of evidence shall not apply to hearings under this section, although the hearing officer shall have the right to exclude evidence which carries no indicia of reliability. All testimony shall be offered under oath or affirmation. Both the city and the licensee shall have the right to subpoena witnesses.
(e) For hearings conducted by a hearing officer, the hearing officer shall issue a report to the mayor and council within ten days of the completion of the hearing. The report shall contain the hearing officer's finding(s) and recommendation(s). Such recommendation(s) shall take into consideration the nature of the violation(s), preventive efforts of the licensee, corrective action taken by the licensee, and the licensee's prior history. Such recommendation(s) may include one or more of the following: suspension of the license for no more than 12 months, revocation of the license, imposition of a probationary period not to exceed 12 months, and/or a civil penalty not to exceed $5,000.00.
(f) The hearing officer's report shall be transmitted to the mayor and council, along with a complete transcript of the hearing. A hearing will be scheduled before the mayor and council. At that hearing the hearing officer may outline the evidence heard and the basis for his recommendation(s). The licensee or its representative may make a statement to the mayor and council in its behalf. Neither side shall introduce any new evidence.
(g) The mayor and council shall determine the penalty or penalties imposed by majority vote of those present and voting. Such penalty may include one or more of the following: suspension for no more than 12 months; probation for no more than 12 months, provided that a licensee currently on probation may have its probation extended for an additional 12 months to begin at the end of the current probationary period; revocation; and/or a civil penalty not to exceed $5,000.00.
(h) The decision of the mayor and council shall be in writing, with the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee within ten days of the hearing date.
(i) A total of three separate and unrelated violations within 24 months, whether or not within the probationary period, shall constitute grounds for permanent revocation.
(Ord. No. 2000-6, § 1, 1-1-2001)

(Ord. No. 96-17, art. IV(A), 5-7-1996)
294:
(a) Pursuant to the authority granted in O.C.G.A. § 36-60-3, and pursuant to the general powers of zoning and land use planning granted to the city council pursuant to the city Charter, adult bookstores, adult movie houses, adult video stores and adult dancing establishments may only be located within areas zoned for commercial or industrial purposes within the city.
(b) No adult bookstore, adult movie house, adult video store or adult dancing establishment shall be located at any place, even if zoned commercial or industrial, if such location is:
(1) Within 1,000 feet of any parcel of real estate which is either zoned for or currently used for residential uses or purposes.
(2) Within 1,000 feet of any parcel of real estate upon which any church, school, governmental building, library, civic center, public park or playground is located.
(3) Within 1,000 feet of any parcel of real estate upon which any other adult bookstore, adult movie house, adult video store or adult dancing establishment is currently located.
(4) Within 1,000 feet of any parcel of real estate upon which is located any business which is currently licensed by the city or any other licensing authority for the purpose of sale of alcoholic beverages to the public, whether such sale is for consumption upon the premises or not.
(5) For purposes of this section, distance shall be by air line measurement from the property line, using the closest property lines of the parcels of land involved. The term "parcel of real estate" means any quantity of land capable of being described by location and boundary, designated and used or to be used as a unit.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. II, 5-7-1996)
Cross reference— Zoning, ch. 74.
295:
Any person or entity holding a retail consumption dealer license for the sale of alcoholic beverages, and any other person, shall be subject to the following rules:
(1) No person shall perform on licensed premises acts of or acts which constitute or simulate:
a. Sexual intercourse, masturbation, sodomy, bestiality, oral copulation, flagellation or any sexual act which is prohibited by law;
b. The touching, caressing or fondling of the breast, buttocks, anus or genitals; or
c. The displaying of any portion of the female breast below the top of the areola or the displaying of any portion of any person's pubic hair, anus, cleft of the buttocks, vulva or genitals.
(2) No person shall use on licensed premises artificial devices or inanimate objects to perform, simulate or depict any of the prohibited conduct or activities described in subsection (1) of this section.
(3) It shall be unlawful for any person to show, display or exhibit, on licensed premises, any film, still picture, electronic reproduction, or any other visual reproduction or image of any act or conduct described in subsection (1) or (2) of this section.
(4) It shall be unlawful for any person employed or working in any capacity in any licensed premises to solicit or encourage patrons to purchase drinks to be consumed by or otherwise disposed of by any such person so employed or working.
(5) No such licensee shall knowingly permit any person in the licensed premises to view from the licensed premises, by glass partition or other artifice, any act or conduct described in subsections (1), (2), (3) and (4) of this section and performed on premises other than the licensed premises.
(6) No such licensee shall knowingly permit any person to remove any alcoholic beverage sold or dispensed on the licensed premises to adjacent or other premises for the purpose of viewing any conduct or activity prohibited on the licensed premises by this article; provided, however, that this section shall not be applicable to a person who removes an alcoholic beverage to his home or place of abode.
(7) It shall be unlawful for any such licensee to employ, encourage, permit or assist any person to engage in any conduct or activity in violation of this article.
(8) The violation of any provision of this article by an alcohol licensee shall constitute grounds for the suspension and revocation of any and all alcoholic beverage licenses issued to such person or entity.
(9) Any person who violates any provision of this section may be cited to appear before the municipal court, and, if found guilty, shall be punished as provided in section 1-11.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. III, 5-7-1996)
Cross reference— Sexual conduct at premises licensed to sell alcoholic beverages, § 6-160.
State Law reference— Similar provisions, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-41 et seq.
296:
(a) The following rules and regulations shall apply to adult dancing establishments:
(1) There shall be no advertisement of adult dancing establishments unless and until a valid permit for such establishment has been issued pursuant to this article.
(2) Each adult dancing establishment shall maintain written records of all employees, including but not limited to all persons employed as dancers, which shall include the names, addresses, social security numbers and dates of birth. At all times, the permittee must maintain such records at the place of business for a period of at least the last two years after the termination of the employment of any person.
(3) No permittee shall employ or contract with any dancer under the age of 18 years.
(4) No person under the age of 18 years shall be admitted to an adult dancing establishment, whether employee or patron.
(5) All adult dancing establishments shall be closed between 12:00 midnight and 8:00 a.m.
(6) No adult dancing establishment permittee shall serve, sell, distribute or allow the consumption or possession of any alcoholic beverage or controlled substance upon the premises of the permittee at any time.
(7) All dancing shall occur on a platform raised at least two feet from the level of the floor.
(8) No dancing shall occur within ten feet of any patron.
(9) No dancer shall have physical contact with any other person while on the premises of the establishment. This prohibition applies to contact with all persons, including patrons and fellow dancers.
(10) No patron shall be allowed to touch any dancer or give any payment or gratuity to any dancer, and no dancer shall solicit any pay or gratuity from any patron.
(b) The following rules and regulations shall apply to all adult entertainment establishments, except in those instances where the rules for adult dancing establishments stated in subsection (a) of this section are in conflict, in which case those rules specifically for adult dancing establishments will apply:
(1) There shall be no visual display, including but not limited to advertisements, which can be seen from outside of the building, which depict nudity or sexual conduct or use words describing nudity or sexual conduct.
(2) No person under the age of 18 years shall be admitted to any adult entertainment establishment. The minimum age for admission to an adult dancing establishment is 18 years.
(3) No adult entertainment establishment permittee shall employ or allow upon the premises for any reason any person under the age of 18 years.
(4) An adult entertainment establishment permittee shall conspicuously display all permits required by this article upon the premises at a place near the entrance.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. VI(A), (B), 5-7-1996; Ord. No. 96-17A, §§ 1, 2, 9-1-1998)
297:
Any adult entertainment establishment operated, conducted or maintained contrary to the provisions of this article is hereby declared to be unlawful and a public nuisance. The city may, in addition to or in lieu of prosecuting a criminal action pursuant to this article, commence legal action for abatement, removal or enjoinment of any such nuisance.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. VI(C), 5-7-1996)
300:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate an adult bookstore, adult movie house, adult video store or adult dancing establishment unless such business shall have a currently valid permit or, if the business has an expired permit, shall have made proper application for renewal within the time required therefor under this article, unless such expired permit was under suspension or permanently or conditionally revoked at the time that it expired. No permit so issued shall condone or make legal any activity thereunder, if such activity is illegal or unlawful under the laws of the state or the United States.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. IV(B), 5-7-1996)
302:
(a) Each application for an adult entertainment establishment permit shall contain the following information:
(1) The applicant's full, true name and any other name used by the applicant during his entire adult life.
(2) The present address and telephone number of the applicant.
(3) The previous addresses of the applicant, if any, for a period of five years immediately prior to the date of the application and the dates of residence at each.
(4) Acceptable documentary proof that the applicant is at least 18 years of age.
(5) The applicant's height, weight, color of eyes and hair and date and place of birth.
(6) Two photographs of the applicant, at least two inches by two inches, taken within the last six months.
(7) Business, occupation or employment history of the applicant for the five years immediately preceding the date of the application.
(8) The business permit history of the applicant, including information relating to previous businesses owned or operated by the applicant in any jurisdiction which required special licenses or permits. Specifically, applicants must disclose full details concerning any license or permit for any adult entertainment business or other licensed or permitted business which was revoked or suspended. Such disclosure must include a full explanation of the reasons for previous revocation or suspension of license or permit.
(9) For each applicant, full disclosure is required as to all convictions, pleas of nolo contendere, or bond forfeitures during the entire life of such applicant, exclusive of traffic violations. For each such matter the applicant must give the date, court and jurisdiction, including a detailed description of the nature of the crime.
(10) If the applicant is a corporation, the name of the corporation shall be set forth exactly as shown in its articles of incorporation or charter, together with the place and date of incorporation, and the names and addresses of each of its current officers and directors, and each stockholder holding more than five percent of the stock in the corporation. If the applicant is a partnership, the applicant shall set forth the name, residence address and dates of birth of the partners, including limited partners. If the applicant is a limited partnership, it shall furnish a copy of its certificate of limited partnership exactly as filed in the superior court. If one or more of the partners is a corporation, the provisions of this subsection pertaining to corporations shall apply. The applicant corporation or partnership shall designate one of its officers or general partners to act as its responsible managing officer. Such designated person shall complete and sign all application forms required of an individual applicant under this article, but only one application fee shall be charged. If the applicant is a corporation, partnership or any business association, full particulars as to each officer, director, partner or shareholder holding five percent of the outstanding issued shares of capital stock must be given in response to each of the items in subsections (1) through (9) of this section.
(11) The name and address of the owner and lessor of the real property upon which the business is to be conducted, and a copy of the lease or rental agreement.
(12) Such other identification and information as the police department may require in order to discover the truth of the matters specified in this section as required to be set forth in the application.
(13) The age and date of birth of the applicant, any partners, any and all officers, any stockholders of more than five percent of the shares of the corporation stock outstanding and directors of the applicant if the applicant is a corporation.
(14) Whether the applicant, any partners or any of the officers or stockholders holding more than five percent of the outstanding shares of the corporation, or the directors of the applicant if the applicant is a corporation, have ever been convicted of any crime constituting a felony, or any crime not a felony, involving moral turpitude in the past five years, and, if so, a complete description of any such crime, including date of violation, date of conviction, jurisdiction and any disposition, including any fine or sentence imposed or whether terms of disposition have been fully completed.
(15) The city shall require the individual applicant to furnish fingerprints of the applicants.
(16) If the applicant is a person doing business under a trade name, a copy of the properly recorded trade number. If the applicant is a corporation, a copy of the authority to do business in the state, including articles of incorporation, trade name affidavit, if any, and last annual report, if any.
(17) At least three character references from individuals who are in no way related to the applicant or individual shareholders, officers or directors of a corporation and who are not or will not benefit financially in any way from the application if the permit is granted and who have not been convicted of any felony or any other crime involving moral turpitude in the past five years. The city clerk shall prepare forms consistent with the provisions of this subsection for the applicant who shall submit all character references on such forms.
(18) The address of the premises to receive the permit.
(19) Whether the premises are owned or rented, and if applicant has a right to legal possession of the premises, copy of those documents giving such legal right.
(20) A plat by a registered engineer, licensed by the state, showing the location of the proposed premises in relation to the neighborhood, the surrounding zoning, its proximity to any church, school, public park, governmental building or site, alcohol sales business or other business regulated under this article.
(b) Each application for an adult entertainment establishment permit shall be verified and acknowledged under oath to be true and correct by:
(1) If the applicant is an individual, the individual;
(2) If a partnership, by the manager or general partner;
(3) If a corporation, by the president of the corporation; or
(4) If any other organization, or association, by the chief administrative official.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. IV(D), 5-7-1996; Ord. No. 96-17A, § 3, 9-1-1998)
303:
No application shall be considered filed until payment of all application fees are received by the city clerk. The city council shall establish a schedule of fees, which shall include an administrative fee for each permit sought, an investigatory fee for each individual to be investigated prior to decision by the city council and a permit fee, which shall be the fee set by the city council for the issuance of each permit. If a permit is denied for any reason, the city clerk shall immediately refund the tendered permit fee. The administrative fee and all investigatory fees shall be nonrefundable.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. IV(E), 5-7-1996)
305:
After the investigatory period has ended, the city clerk shall place the issue upon the agenda of the next regularly scheduled meeting of the city council, at which time a hearing shall be conducted. Such hearings shall follow the normal administrative procedures, with the mayor or mayor pro tempore acting as chairperson. The applicant will be permitted to appear and make an oral presentation and present documentary evidence and testimony in support of the application. Questions may be addressed to the applicant or any other person who appears before the city council. A decision shall be reached by the city council by the close of business on the next business day following the conclusion of the hearing. A written notice of decision, including the reason for any denial, shall be mailed to the applicant at the address shown on the application.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. V(B), 5-7-1996)
306:
Permits for adult entertainment establishments may be renewed on an annual basis, provided that the permittees continue to meet all of the requirements set out in this article. The city clerk will provide a form for an application for renewal. If any facts have changed since the initial application for the permit, full particulars as to any such change must be given in the same form as an initial application for permit. The renewal fee shall be established by resolution of the city council from time to time. All fees owed to the city, including the renewal fee and any other type of administrative fee, utility bill, fine or any other type indebtedness owed to the city, must be paid before the issuance of a renewal permit.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. V(C), 5-7-1996)
307:
No adult entertainment establishment permit may be sold, transferred or assigned by a permittee. This absolute prohibition against transfer applies to voluntary sales, transfers by operation of law, inheritance, automatic transfer to a bankruptcy trustee or other fiduciary or levy by creditors. If the permittee named in the permit issued ceases to do business under that permit in that location for any reason, the permit shall be automatically canceled and thereafter null and void. However, if the permittee is a partnership, and one or more of the partners should die, the surviving partner or partners may acquire, by purchase or otherwise, the interest of the deceased partner or partners without affecting a surrender or termination of such permit. In such case, the surviving partner may obtain a renewal of the permit in his own separate name from the city clerk, provided that the surviving partner is not otherwise disqualified from holding the permit.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. V(C), 5-7-1996)
308:
A permit shall be issued for each physical location of an adult entertainment establishment. After a permit is issued, it shall not be valid for any adult entertainment operated in any other location than that specified on the permit. Therefore, if an applicant wishes to relocate, the entire application procedure shall be recommenced as if no permit had ever been issued.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. V(D), 5-7-1996)
309:
The city council retains authority to revoke any permit issued under this article. If the city council believes that there is any failure to maintain any of the qualifications to hold a permit, any variance between the permitted use and the actual use in violation of this article, any material misrepresentation in any application which was not discovered until after the permit was granted, any violation of any provision of this article or any other reason to believe that the continued operation of an adult entertainment establishment is harmful to the health, morals, peace and dignity of the community, then it shall issue to the permittee a notice of hearing. The notice shall include sufficient information for the permittee to prepare its defense and shall notify the permittee of the time and date of the hearing before the city council wherein the issue of revocation of the permit shall be decided. Such hearing shall be no less than ten days following the date that the notice is mailed to the address of the permittee. At the hearing, the permittee will be allowed to present evidence and examine any witness or evidence submitted before the city council. Following the hearing, the city council shall issue its written decision within a reasonable period of time and mail a copy to the permittee. Any adverse decision shall include specific reasons for such decision. The city council may order any of the following:
(1) The permit may be continued without alteration;
(2) The permit may be modified so as to place reasonable restrictions upon the permittee's conduct of business for a reasonable period of time so as to deter or prevent a repeat of the type of conduct that led to the disciplinary action; or
(3) The permit may be revoked, effective immediately.
(Ord. No. 96-17, art. VI(D), 5-7-1996)
312:
It shall be a privilege for the owner or operator of a business location within the city to offer bona fide coin operated amusement machines to the public at the business location. No business owner or business operator shall offer to the public more than nine Class B bona fide coin operated amusement machines that reward the player exclusively with noncash merchandise, prizes, toys, gift certificates, or novelties at the same business location.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
313:
It shall be the duty of every owner or operator of a business location that rewards the player exclusively as described in subsection (d) of O.C.G.A. Section 16-12-35 to inform all employees of the prohibitions and penalties set out in subsections (3), (f), and (g) of O.C.G.A. Section 16-12-35.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
314:
It shall be the duty of every owner or possessor of any bona fide coin operated amusement machine that rewards the player exclusively as described in subsection (d) of O.C.G.A. Section 16-12-35 to inform each business owner or business operator of the business location where such machine is located of the prohibitions and penalties set out in subsections (e), (f), and (g) of O.C.G.A. Section 16-12-35.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
315:
Conviction of a violation of subsections (e), (f), or (g) of O.C.G.A. Section 16-12-35 by and owner, operator, or employee of a business location offering to the public any bona fide coin operated amusement machine for which business location an alcoholic beverage license has been issued to the City of Jackson, pursuant to chapter 6 of this Code, shall be grounds for the suspension, revocation, or refusal to renew such alcoholic beverage license. Any adverse action against a licensee shall be brought in accordance with section 6-190 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
316:
It shall be the duty of any business owner or business operator offering to the public bona fide coin operated amusement machines at the business location to provide to the mayor, or his designee, a copy of each verified monthly report prepared in accordance with O.C.G.A. Section 48-17-15, the provisions of which are incorporated herein by reference, together with the penalties authorized by subsection (d) of O.C.G.A. Section 48-17-15.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
317:
The owner or operator of any business location at which bona fide coin operated amusement machines are offered to the public shall place and maintain the machines in plain view in an area of the business location accessible to any person in the business location.
It shall be the duty of every owner or operator of a business location which offers to the public one or more bona fide coin operated amusement machines to prominently and conspicuously post a notice, in block letters not less than two inches in height, within ten feet of at least one machine, including the following language:
"GEORGIA LAW PROHIBITS PAYMENT OR RECEIPT OF MONEY FOR WINNING A GAME OR GAMES ON THIS AMUSEMENT MACHINE; PAYMENT OR RECEIPT OF MONEY FOR FREE REPLAYS WON ON THIS AMUSEMENT MACHINE; PAYMENT OR RECEIPT OF MONEY FOR ANY MERCHANDISE, PRIZE, TOY, GIFT CERTIFICATE, OR NOVELTY WON ON THIS AMUSEMENT MACHINE; OR AWARDING ANY MERCHANDISE, PRIZE, TOY, GIFT CERTIFICATE, OR NOVELTY OF A VALUE EXCEEDING $5.00 FOR A SINGLE PLAY OF THIS MACHINE."
In addition thereto, it shall be the further duty of the owner or operator of a business location to conspicuously post within the place of business its occupation tax certificate, any business or regulatory licenses held for the business at that location including alcoholic beverage license, if any, and the name, address and contact information for the owner of any bona fide coin operated amusement machines located upon the premises.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)
318:
The owner or operator of any business location in violation of this article shall be entitled to at least 30 days written notice setting forth the facts of the violation with sufficient specificity. For a first violation, the owner or operator voluntarily curing the violation(s) shall cause the notice to be reduced to a warning; provided, however, consideration of the violation may be used in furtherance of sanctions for any subsequent violations.
The notice shall be served on the business owner or operator by personal service if the person, firm, corporation or other business entity is resident within Butts County, Georgia, otherwise by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address shown on the business' occupation tax certificate, if a non-resident of Butts County, Georgia. A business owner or operator may request a hearing within the 30 days following service of the notice. The hearing shall be conducted by the mayor and council or a hearing officer appointed by the mayor; the hearing officer shall be an attorney licensed in this state who is disinterested in the proceedings. Hearings shall only be as formal as necessary to preserve order and shall be compatible with the principles of justice. The hearing officer shall make his or her final written determination within ten days of the completion of the hearing.
If the hearing officer concludes this article has been violated, the mayor may impose a civil penalty not to exceed $500.00 for the first infraction, and a civil penalty not to exceed $1,000.00 for each subsequent infraction. For a third or subsequent infraction, the privilege of offering bona fide coin operated amusement machines at the business location may be revoked or suspended.
(Ord. No. 2012-10-01, § 1, 11-6-2012)

323:
(a) It shall be unlawful to ride horses, mules, ponies and any other animal upon the sidewalks, roadways or rights-of-way in the city. The city may make exceptions to the preceding sentence for permitted parades.
(b) Violation of this article shall be punishable, upon conviction, as provided in section 1-11.
(Ord. of 5-20-1986(2))
State Law reference— Livestock running at large, O.C.G.A. § 4-3-1 et seq.
324:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to have or keep, to pasture, or confine within the corporate limits of the city any horses, mules, donkeys, burros, ponies, cows, calves, sheep or goats.
(b) Domestic chickens are only allowed within R-15, R-20, and R-30 Zoning Classifications. Only four chickens are allowed to be kept, and they must be always confined to a cage, coop, corral, or similar enclosure that has four sides, a top, and a secure latch to keep the chickens from running at large, even within a fence in backyard. The chicken cage, coop, corral, or similar enclosures are only permitted in the backyard, it shall be prohibited to be in the front interior side or corner side yard of the residential lot. All roosters are prohibited. All food supplies maintained for the coop shall be kept in a secure and rodent-proof container. All other fowl such as ducks, turkeys, geese, guinea fowl, pea fowl, peacocks, pigeons, doves, quail or any birds of prey are strictly prohibited anywhere within the city limits.
(c) Any person found to be in violation of this section shall be punished, upon conviction, according to section 1-11.
(Ord. of 3-20-1978; Res. of 1-16-2007; Ord. No. 2025-003, 4-1-2025)
327:
Footnote 2:
State Law reference— Animal bites, O.C.G.A. § 31-19-4; Dangerous Dog Control Law, O.C.G.A. § 4-8-20 et seq.; liability of owner or keeper of vicious or dangerous animal for injuries caused by animal, O.C.G.A. § 51-2-7.
328:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Dangerous dogs means any dogs who are on record with any law enforcement agency, animal control agency, local, state or federal court or a dog control officer for having bitten or endangering a human being without provocation, except dogs used by law enforcement officers, or dogs who attack in response to willful trespass or other tort. Dogs who attack in response to torment, abuse or assault shall not be included in this section within the meaning of a dangerous dog.
Dog control officer means a person appointed by the county board of commissioners by and through the director of the county environmental department, along with all police officers of the city, who are given the authority and responsibility for making whatever investigations or inquiries are necessary to locate and identify classified dogs who are potentially dangerous or dangerous.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog that has the potential for biting human beings on public or private property or chasing human beings in a vicious manner on public grounds without provocation.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 4.1; Amend. of 4-4-2000)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
329:
The mayor and the city council, in furtherance of their responsibility to protect the public health, safety and well-being of the citizens, enact this article providing for requirements to classify and regulate dangerous or potentially dangerous dogs and to establish certain conditions for the ownership of such dogs.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989)
330:
(a) The county animal control officer shall serve as the dog control officer of the city in the enforcement of this article, along with all police officers of the city.
(b) The mayor and city council shall name by appropriate resolution a dog control officer or any number of dog control officers required to enforce this article.
(c) The dog control officer or officers shall be authorized to issue citations to any violators.
(Res. of 2-6-1989; Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 6.0; Amend. of 4-4-2000)
331:
(a) Dangerous dog owners who violate this article are guilty of a misdemeanor. Upon conviction of the violation of this article, the owner shall be fined a minimum of $100.00 for the first conviction, $500.00 for the second conviction, $750.00 for the third conviction and $1,000.00 for a fourth or subsequent conviction. No fines may be suspended in whole or in part.
(b) Potentially dangerous dog owners who violate this article are guilty of a misdemeanor. Upon the first conviction, the owner shall be required to pay a fine in the amount of $50.00, upon the second conviction the fine of $150.00, upon the third conviction the fine of $300.00 and upon the fourth conviction the fine of $1,000.00. No fines shall be suspended in whole or in part.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 5.3)
332:
(a) Violations tried upon citations. Violations of this article shall be tried upon citations, before the municipal court, with or without a prosecuting attorney. The city attorney may serve as a prosecuting attorney.
(b) Warrants issued if felony is charged. The dog control officer shall be entitled to have warrants taken as provided in O.C.G.A. §§ 4-8-4—4-8-29 if felony charges are warranted by those O.C.G.A. sections.
(c) Civil remedies. The dog control officer shall also be entitled to any civil remedies for injunctions, or restraints provided by the superior court.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 6.1)
333:
(a) Complaint; investigation; notification of owner of classification and right of appeal. When any complaint concerning a potentially dangerous or dangerous dog has been filed with the dog control officer, or if he has received information concerning the attack of a dog on a human being, the officer shall, after any investigation and injuries, notify the owner by certified mail concerning the facts of his investigation that the animal has been classified as a potentially dangerous dog and what requirements the owner shall be expected to meet. The officer shall also notify the owner that he may request a hearing to contest the classification within 15 days from receipt of the notice. If no hearing is requested, the dog's classification shall go into effect on the 15th day.
(b) Hearing by board of health or animal control board. If the owner requests a hearing contesting the classification of his dog to that of a potentially dangerous or dangerous dog, a hearing must be provided within 30 days of the receipt of the request by the dog control officer. The city may designate the board of health to conduct such hearings or may create by resolution or ordinance an animal control board to hold hearings. If an animal control board is created, the dog control officer or anyone else involved in dog classification cannot sit on such board.
(c) Notification of owner of hearing date; presentation of evidence; final determination. The owner must be notified of the hearing date and location by certified mail. During the hearings, the owner may have the opportunity to present any evidence or testimony on their behalf. The final determination must be provided by the city or its duly appointed representative within ten days of the hearing by certified mail to the owner. If the animal is to be given the classification as dangerous or potentially dangerous the effective date of such classification must be given.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 5.0; Amend. of 4-4-2000)
335:
The dog control officer is authorized to make whatever inquiries are necessary to ensure compliance among dangerous and potentially dangerous dog owner of the items listed in this article. The City of Jackson Police Department and City of Jackson Code Enforcement are required to cooperate. Dogs that are not maintained in compliance with this article must be confiscated by the dog control officer.
(1) The owner must notify the dog control officer within 24 hours if the dog is on the loose, is unconfined, has attacked a person, has died, or has been sold or donated.
(2) The owner must keep the dog in an enclosure unless such dog is restrained by a strong leash and accompanied by a responsible person. Dangerous dogs must also be muzzled.
(3) The owner must maintain all registration requirements including liability insurance or a surety bond.
(4) Dogs that have been confiscated are to be held for 20 days. The owner may reclaim their dogs by complying with requirements and paying a confiscation fee as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, which are on file in the city hall, as well as any expenses incurred in caring for the dog. If the dog has not been reclaimed by its owner within 20 days, the dog shall be destroyed in an expeditious and humane manner.
(Ord. of 2-6-1989, § 5.2; Ord. No. 01-04-2008, § 2, 4-15-2008)
338:
It shall be unlawful for any person to keep, maintain or confine swine of any kind, in any number or in any manner, within the city.
(Ord. No. 96-15, art. I(A), 5-7-1996)
339:
The provisions of section 10-61 shall not apply to Vietnamese potbellied miniature pigs ("potbellied pigs") that are maintained as household pets. However, to maintain a potbellied pig as a pet, the following requirements, restrictions and conditions shall apply:
(1) All potbellied pigs that are maintained within the city limits must be registered with the city clerk within 14 days from the time the pig is taken to its place of residence. Such registration shall constitute a permit to keep and maintain potbellied miniature pigs within the city limits. Such registration shall include the name, address and telephone number of the owner, location of the pig, identification number and description of the pig and a health certificate. All potbellied pigs must have permanent identification numbers by either ear tag, fire brand, freeze brand or tattoo.
(2) The owner of a potbellied pig must inform the city clerk within ten days of the death, change in ownership or change in location of such animal.
(3) It shall be unlawful to keep, harbor, maintain or raise more than two potbellied pigs in any location within the city limits.
(4) All such potbellied pigs over six months of age must be blood tested by an accredited veterinarian and certified free of brucellosis and pseudo-rabies when first registered and again upon each change of ownership. It shall be the responsibility of the owner of the pig to provide to the city clerk the initial health certificate and all change of ownership health certificates from an accredited veterinarian, which shall include the following:
a. The name and address of the owner;
b. The name, address and telephone number of the accredited veterinarian;
c. Identification number and description of the animal;
d. Certification that the animal is free of brucellosis and pseudo-rabies and date of last blood test; and
e. Statement of general health of animal.
(5) For purposes of this section, potbellied pigs that are kept or maintained within the city limits cannot exceed 18 inches in height at shoulder level or weigh more than 100 pounds. All potbellied pigs in excess of such height and weight restrictions are prohibited.
(6) All potbellied pigs within the city limits must be under the owner's control and restraint by either a fenced enclosure or on a leash.
(7) The breeding of potbellied pigs for any reason or purpose is strictly prohibited within the city limits.
(8) All locations where potbellied pigs are kept shall be kept in a clean and sanitary condition. Exercise areas shall be cleaned of excrement on a daily basis and continuously maintained in such manner as not to cause, by odor or noise, material distress, discomfort or injury to persons of ordinary sensibilities in the immediate vicinity thereof.
(Ord. No. 96-15, art. I(B), 5-7-1996)
340:
Any violation, disobedience, omission, neglect, failure or refusal to comply with the enforcement of any of the provisions of this article may result in the revocation of the permit to maintain such potbellied pigs within the city limits. Any person violating this article may be cited to appear before the municipal court and, upon conviction of any violation of this article, may be punished as provided in section 1-11.
(Ord. No. 96-15, art. I(C), 5-7-1996)

343:
In order to protect the health and safety of persons and animals in the city, to improve and make for safe motor vehicle and pedestrian traffic, to control the incidence and spread of rabies, to prohibit abandonment and other forms of cruelty to animals, to promote the general welfare of the citizens of this city by providing specific regulations concerning the care and treatment of animals and providing for violations of those regulations, and to invest the authority to enforce those regulations, the council hereby adopts this article.
The City of Jackson Code Enforcement Officer, Public Works Director, and any police officer can issue warnings and citations for any unlawful act defined in section 10-89 of this chapter but only when no physical contact with the animal is required and not for transporting the animal or when animals that are dangerous or suspected to be dangerous are involved.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 1, 4-4-2000; Ord. No. 2023-004, 3-7-2023)
344:
The animal control department shall be under the direction of the county board of commissioners, by and through the director of the county environmental department. Its agents shall be charged with the responsibility of enforcing the animal control ordinance of the city and the operation of the county animal shelter.
While the animal control department shall be under the direction of the county board of commissioners, there is nothing in this chapter that prevents the local jurisdiction and the agents of the jurisdiction to make contact to communicate about animals through visits, letters, warnings, citations, emails, or phone calls. This communication can address any unlawful acts defined in section 10-89, except those which involve physical contact with the animal, transporting the animal, or when animals are dangerous or suspected to be dangerous or diseased.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 2, 4-4-2000; Ord. No. 2023-004, 3-7-2023)
345:
For the purpose of this article, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section:
Abandoned animal shall mean any animal which shall have been placed upon public property or within a public building unattended and uncared for, or upon or within the private property of another without the express permission of the owner, custodian or tenant of the private property and is unattended or without care. An animal shall also be considered as abandoned, for the purposes of this article, which has been upon or within the property of the owner or custodian of this animal for a period of time in excess of 36 hours unattended and without proper food, water and shelter. Abandonment shall also include failure to provide reasonable remedy or relief for any injured or diseased animal.
Animal shall be defined as follows and shall be limited to only those animals which are allowed to be kept within the corporate boundaries of the city by city ordinance or state law:
Domestic animals: Animals that are accustomed to live in or about the habitation of humans, that are not found naturally in the wild state.
Domestic/wild animals: An established strain of wild animal which is generally used in the fur or pet industry.
Feral animals: Domestic animals which have reverted back to a wild state and do not exhibit traits consistent with their intended use.
Native wildlife animals: A nondomesticated animal which is normally found in the natural state within the confines of Georgia.
Non-native or exotic wildlife animals: A nondomesticated animal which is not normally found in the natural state within the confines of Georgia.
Animal control officer shall mean any person designated by the county board of commissioners by and through the director of the county environmental department to enforce the provisions of this article. This is also any agent of the City of Jackson who is charged with addressing unlawful acts involving animals.
Animal nuisance shall mean any animal which: (1) is dangerous; (2) causes unsanitary conditions; (3) attacks passersby or passing vehicles; (4) is found at large and not under restraint three or more times within a 12-month period; (5) damages property of others; (6) excessively produces disturbing noises; (7) is a female dog while in estrus (in heat, in season) not restrained in a manner which can reasonably be expected to keep away or not attract male dogs; or (8) is inimical to the public health, welfare or safety according to the rules and regulations promulgated by the county board of health, which rules and regulations are incorporated herein and made a part hereof as if fully set out in this chapter.
Animal shelter or pound shall mean the facilities operated by the county for confining animals impounded or surrendered under the provisions of this article.
Animal under restraint means: (a) any animal secured by a leash or lead with a collar, or under supervision of a responsible and competent person at least 16 years of age, and obedient to the person's commands; (b) a dog being trained or hunted in conformance with the game laws of the state or those dogs considered to be work animals.
Certificate shall mean a certificate or document issued at the time of vaccination for rabies of a dog or cat and bearing thereon the signature of the vaccinator, the vaccination tag number, the name, color, breed and sex of the dog or cat, the name and address of the owner, and the date of the vaccination.
Current vaccination tag shall mean a metal tag issued by the state department of human resources, or other state agency, which bears a number showing that it is current for a period of one year up to three years for immunization of rabies.
Dangerous animal means an animal whose owner knows or reasonably should know presents a danger to humans or other animals because: (a) it has, without provocation, bitten or attacked a person or another animal in the past; (b) it has exhibited threatening or vicious conduct or propensities toward humans or other animals, or (c) it qualifies as a "dangerous dog" as that term is defined at O.C.G.A. § 4-8-21(a)(1).
Fence means a structure of wire, wood, stone, or other materials which is of sufficient height and strength to act as a barrier against passage of the animal or animals it is intended to enclose. "Fence" also includes so-called "invisible fence" systems which provide an electric shock which prevents an animal from leaving the property of its owner, provided the animal is a dog which is neither dangerous nor in estrus. (Dogs which are dangerous as defined in this section shall be restrained in an enclosure which not only restrains the animal from leaving the owner's property, but also protects persons who may come onto the property from harm. Female dogs in estrus (in heat, in season) shall be confined in a conventional enclosure or otherwise restrained in a way which prevents breeding not intended by the owner.)
Guard dog shall mean any dog which has been trained to attack persons or other animals independently or upon oral command and any dog which, while not so trained, is reasonably expected to perform as a guardian of the property upon and/or within which it is located.
Humane manner shall mean to provide care for an animal to include, but not necessarily limited to, adequate heat, ventilation and sanitary shelter or manner of restraint, wholesome food and water consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, species and breed; also providing of necessary veterinary medical care to insure reasonable thriftiness and relief from undue pain or suffering.
Inhumane manner means the failure to provide humane care and shall also mean restraining an animal by affixing to its collar or otherwise attaching to its body a chain, rope, cord, or other lead which is attached to the ground or a fixed object and which is not of sufficient length to allow the animal access to food and water or to move about freely in an area of reasonable size considering the size and nature of the animal.
Owner shall mean any person owning, keeping, harboring or acting as custodian or an animal for a period of 72 hours or more.
Person shall mean an individual, firm, corporation, municipality, society, or owner.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog that has the potential for biting human beings on public or private property or chasing human beings in a vicious manner on public grounds without provocation at any time after February 6, 1989.
Vaccinate shall mean the proper administration, by a licensed veterinarian, of a specified dose of antirabies vaccine into a dog or cat, such vaccine having the U.S. license number approval stamped on the label of the vaccine container and having been approved by the state department of human resources, or other state agency.
Veterinarian shall mean any person who holds a license to practice the profession of veterinary medicine in the state.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 3, 4-4-2000; Ord. No. 2023-004, 3-7-2023)
346:
It shall be the duty of each dog or cat owner, possessor, or custodian thereof, to provide a collar for their dog or cat to which a current rabies vaccination tag shall be attached. The collar, together with the tag, shall be worn by the dog or cat at all times, except as provided herein. Failure to comply with this section shall be unlawful and shall be punished as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 4, 4-4-2000)
347:
Enforcement of this article shall be carried out substantially as follows:
(1) The primary responsibility for the enforcement of this article shall be vested in the county board of commissioners, by and through the director of the county environmental department. The director of the environmental department may be designated by the county board of health as the official rabies control authority. Upon information made known to or complaint lodged with the director or his authorized representative, that any owner, possessor or custodian of any dog or animal is in violation of this article, the director or his authorized representative shall investigate such information or complaint. The director shall not be required to respond to anonymous complaints. In the event that the owner, possessor or custodian of any dog or animal is not known and a dog or animal is upon the public streets, alleys, sidewalks, school grounds or other public places or premises, or upon the property of another without that property owner's permission, upon complaint made to or information made known to the animal control division of the environmental department, it shall be the duty of the director or his authorized representative to immediately take possession of this dog or animal and impound it as herein provided.
(2) Jackson Code Enforcement Officer, Public Works Director, or police officer can enforce all local ordinances including those related to animals except those which involve physical contact with the animal, transporting the animal, or when animals are dangerous or suspected to be dangerous or diseased.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 5, 4-4-2000; Ord. No. 2023-004, 3-7-2023)
348:
The county animal control officers are hereby authorized to impound any dangerous dog or guard dog not confined, chained or muzzled as herein provided; any female dog while in estrus (in heat, in season) not restrained within an enclosure, which can reasonably be expected to keep away or not attract male dogs; any animal not wearing the rabies inoculation tag required by the statutes of the state; and any animal deemed to be a nuisance in the city. The animal shall be confined in the animal shelter or handled as otherwise provided herein.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 6, 4-4-2000)
349:
Upon impounding any dog or other animal, the county board of commissioners, by and through the director of the county environmental department or its authorized representative, shall cause to be made a prompt and reasonable effort to locate the animal's owner, possessor or custodian. Upon location thereof, notification of impounding shall be sent to this owner, possessor or custodian. For the purpose of this section, it shall be deemed sufficient notice if a notification of impounding is sent by certified mail to the owner named on the most recent rabies certificate on file at the address indicated thereon within three days. If the dog or animal is not claimed by the owner, possessor or custodian thereof within the time hereinafter specified, or if the impounded dog or animal is not wearing a rabies tag or a tag identifying the name, address and telephone number of the owner, possessor or custodian, then and in that event, the director or his authorized representative may dispose of the dog or animal as provided herein. Animals deemed in pain and suffering or to be diseased with contagious pathogens may be sacrificed expeditiously.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 7, 4-4-2000)
350:
The personnel of the animal control shelter shall not release any animal impounded until the owner of said animal has paid all fees and charges assessed, and until the owner has prepaid for a rabies tag or tags as required by state law and by county health department rules. The fees and fines shall be established by the council and shall be amended from time to time.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 8, 4-4-2000)
351:
(a) Any animal which has been impounded, and is not reclaimed by its owner within seven calendar days of the date impounded, shall be subject to adoption, or to euthanasia by humane methods by the personnel of the animal control shelter. If such animal is adopted by a person other than its owner, it may be released upon prepayment of the cost of rabies vaccination and tags where applicable and an adoption fee.
(b) Surrendered animals may be made available for adoption immediately, and the above fees shall apply.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 9, 4-4-2000)
352:
(a) The owner or possessor of each dog or cat over four months of age kept, maintained or harbored within the city or the unincorporated areas of the county shall apply for and obtain a rabies tag for such dog or cat which shall be affixed to a collar worn by such dog or cat at all times. This provision does not apply to show dogs or cats wherein the wearing of a collar may cause damage to the coat of the animal. Owners of show dogs or cats shall have in their possession the rabies tag where it may be produced on demand of animal control personnel.
(b) Proceeds from the sale of licenses and shelter fees shall be applied to the general operating budget of the county.
(c) Any licensed veterinarian shall be authorized to vaccinate dogs or cats against rabies; provided that at the time of such vaccination he furnish a vaccination tag issued by the state department of human resources, bearing an official serial number, to the owner. He shall furnish a certificate or certificates certifying to the vaccination of each dog or cat, sending one copy to the county animal control division and keeping a copy for his files.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any person to attach a vaccination tag or license tag to the collar of any animal for which it was not issued.
(e) A license fee shall be charged for the certificate of registration as required by chapter 8 of title 4 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A. § 4-8-25) for a potentially dangerous dog.
(f) A license fee shall be charged for a certificate of registration as required by chapter 8 of title 4 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A. § 4-8-25) for a dangerous dog.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 10, 4-4-2000)
353:
It shall be the duty of any person knowing of a rabid animal, or of an animal showing rabid symptoms, to immediately report such animal to the animal control shelter and give as much pertinent information as possible.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 11, 4-4-2000)
354:
(a) Where rabies has been found to exist in any animal, or where its existence is suspected, the director of the county environmental department may designate an area within which quarantine of all such animals shall be maintained and all such animals shall thereupon be immediately confined to the premises designated by the director of the environmental department in a manner approved by state and county health officials, whether or not such animal has been vaccinated against rabies.
(b) No animal shall be removed from or brought into a quarantined area or premises without prior approval of the director of the county environmental department.
(c) Quarantine ordered by the director of the county environmental department shall be maintained for such period as the director of the environmental department deems necessary to protect the public health.
(d) Quarantined areas or premises, and areas where rabid animals or animals suspected of rabies remain at large, shall be posted by the director of the county environmental department with signs which read as follows: "Rabies Suspected" or "Rabies—Keep Away From Animals." Such signs shall be conspicuously displayed in a place designated by the director of the environmental department and shall not be defaced or removed except by the director of the environmental department. Signs furnished and approved by the director of the environmental department shall be used.
(e) The owner or custodian of each animal subject to a quarantine invoked by the director of the county environmental department under terms of this regulation shall be notified of the quarantine, the particular animals subject thereto, and shall be given such other information as the director of the environmental department deems necessary.
(f) The heads of all animals having had rabies or suspected of having had rabies at time of death shall be submitted to the director of the county environmental department for examination by the department of human resources laboratory. When necessary, the director of the environmental department can sacrifice an animal for the purpose of submitting brain tissue for rabies analysis.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 12, 4-4-2000)
355:
Any person violating the terms of this article shall be punished in the municipal court of the city as provided in section 1-11 for each separate violation.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 13, 4-4-2000)
356:
No injunction or claim for damage may be filed against the city, its officers and employees, or the animal control division and its employees for alleged wrong-doing arising from the enforcement of this article except upon court order after due notice and proper hearing.
(Ord. No. 2000-2, § 14, 4-4-2000)
358:
For local violations (not regulated through Butts County Animal Control), the first violation that results in a citation will have a fine of $50.00 that will be charged to the owner of the animal or the owner/renter of the home where the animal is kept or is being kept. The second violation will have a fine of $100.00 that will be charged to the owner of the animal or the owner/renter of the home where the animal permanently lives or is being temporarily housed.
Further violations will be a court appearance only and the judge will determine the fine not to exceed the maximum for code enforcement violations.
If there are multiple owners of one animal, each owner may receive a citation. If an owner cannot be established, the violation will be directed to the owner or renter where the animal permanently lives or is being temporarily housed.
(Ord. No. 2023-004, 3-7-2023)

366:
The purpose of this section is to provide for the administration and enforcement of the Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes for Construction as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs. Hereinafter, the state minimum standard codes for construction shall be referred to as "the construction codes."
(Ord. of 3-6-2018)
367:
(a) General. These construction codes are hereby declared to be remedial, and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof - which are public safety, health, and general welfare - through structural strength, stability, sanitation, adequate light and ventilation, and safety to life and property from fire and other hazards attributed to the built environment including alteration, repair, removal, demolition, use, and occupancy of buildings, structures, or premises, and by regulating the installation and maintenance of all electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems, which may be referred to as service systems.
(b) Quality control. Quality control of materials and workmanship is not within the purview of the construction codes except as it relates to the purposes stated therein.
(c) Permitting and inspection. The inspection or permitting of any building, system, or plan, under the requirements of construction codes shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building, system or plan or their adequacy. The city of Jackson, nor any employee thereof, shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building, system or plan, nor for any failure of any component of such, which may occur subsequent to such inspection or permitting.
(Ord. of 3-6-2018)
368:
(a) Applicability.
(1) General. Where, in any specific case, different sections of these construction codes specify different materials, methods of construction, or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern. Where there is a conflict between a general requirement and a specific requirement, the specific requirement shall be applicable.
(2) Building. The provisions of the International Building Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to the construction, alteration, repair, equipment, use and occupancy, location, maintenance, removal, and demolition, of every building or structure or any appurtenances connected or attached to such buildings or structures, except in one- and two-family dwellings.
(3) Electrical. The provisions of the National Electrical Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to the installation of electrical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances thereto.
(4) Gas. The provisions of the International Fuel Gas Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to the installation of consumer's gas piping, gas appliances, and related accessories as covered in this Code. These requirements apply to gas piping systems extending from the point of delivery to the inlet connections of appliances and the installation and operation of residential and commercial gas appliances and related accessories, except in one- and two-family dwellings.
(5) Mechanical. The provisions of the International Mechanical Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to the installation of mechanical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings and/or appurtenances, including ventilating, heating, cooling, air conditioning and refrigeration systems, incinerators, and other energy related systems, except in one- and two-family dwellings.
(6) Plumbing. The provisions of the International Plumbing Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to every plumbing installation, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances, and when connected to a water or sewerage system.
(7) One and two-family dwellings. In addition to those codes referenced herein, the provisions of the International Residential Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall apply to the building, mechanical, and gas systems in new one- and two-family dwellings, including additions, alterations, renovations and general repairs of existing one- and two-family dwellings.
(8) Energy. The provisions of the International Energy Conservation Code, as adopted and amended by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs, shall regulate the design of building envelopes for adequate thermal resistance and low air leakage and the design and selection of mechanical, electrical, service water heating, and illumination systems and equipment that will enable the effective use of energy in new building construction.
(b) Federal and state authority. The provisions of the construction codes shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency, or any applicable governing authority having jurisdiction, of any power or authority which it had on the effective date of the adoption of the construction codes or of any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive any individual or corporation of its legal rights as provided by law.
(c) Appendices. Any appendices referenced in Article I of this Chapter shall be considered an integral part of the construction codes.
(d) Referenced standards. Standards referenced in the text of the construction codes shall be considered an integral part of the construction codes. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Where construction code provisions conflict with a standard, the construction code provisions shall be enforced. Permissive and advisory provisions in a standard shall not be construed as mandatory.
(e) Maintenance. All buildings, structures, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems, both existing and new, and all parts thereof, shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition. All devices or safeguards, which are required by the construction codes when constructed, altered, or repaired, shall be maintained in good working order. The owner, or his/her designated agent, shall be responsible for the maintenance of buildings, structures, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems.
(Ord. of 3-6-2018)
369:
(a) General. Alterations, repairs, or rehabilitation work may be made to any existing structure, building, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system without requiring the building, structure, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or gas system to comply with all the requirements of the construction codes provided that the alteration, repair, or rehabilitation work conforms to the requirements of the construction codes for new construction. The building official shall determine the extent to which the existing system shall be made to conform to the requirements of the construction codes for new construction.
(b) Change of occupancy. If the occupancy classification of any existing building or structure is changed, the building, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems shall be made to conform to the intent of the construction codes as required by the building official.
(c) Special historic buildings. The provisions of the construction codes relating to the construction, alteration, repair, enlargement, restoration, relocation, or moving of buildings or structures shall not be mandatory for existing buildings or structures identified and classified by the state or local jurisdiction as historic buildings when such buildings or structures are judged by the building official to be safe and in the public interest of health, safety, and welfare regarding any proposed construction, alteration, repair, enlargement, restoration, relocation, or moving of buildings within the fire districts.
(Ord. of 3-6-2018)
370:
(a) Creation of building department. There is hereby established a department to be called the building department and the person in charge shall be known as the building official. The governing body shall establish the qualifications for the building official and other code enforcement personnel. The duties of the department may be contracted out in full to a third party entity.
(b) Restrictions on employees. An officer or employee connected with the department, except one whose only connection is as a member of the construction board of adjustment and appeal, shall not be financially interested in the furnishing of labor, material, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building, structure, service, system, or in the making of plans or of specifications thereof, unless he is the owner of such. This officer or employee shall not engage in any other work, which is inconsistent with his duties or conflict with the interests of the department.
(c) Records. The building official shall keep, or cause to be kept, a record of the business of the department. The records of the department shall be open to public inspection pursuant to the provisions of the Georgia Open Records Act.
(d) Liability. Any officer or employee, or member of the construction board of appeals, charged with the enforcement of the construction codes, acting for the applicable governing authority in the discharge of his duties, shall not thereby render himself/herself personally liable, and is hereby relieved from all personal liability, for any damage that may occur to persons or property as a result of any act required or permitted in the discharge of his/her duties. Any suit brought against any officer or employee or member because of such act performed by him/her in the enforcement of any provision of the construction codes shall be defended by the governing jurisdiction until the final termination of the proceedings.
(e) Reports. The building official shall submit a report each year covering the work of the building department during the preceding year. He/she may incorporate in said report a summary of the decisions of the construction board of appeals during said year.
(Ord. of 3-6-2018)
371:
(a) General. The building official is hereby authorized and directed to enforce the provisions of the construction codes. The building official is further authorized to render interpretations of the construction codes, which are consistent with its intent and purpose. The city may contract with a third party to provide the duties of the building official.
(b) Right of entry.
(1) Whenever necessary to make an inspection to enforce any of the provisions of the construction codes, or whenever the building official has reasonable cause to believe that there exists in any building or upon any premises any condition or code violation which makes such building, structure, premises, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems unsafe, dangerous, or hazardous, the building official may enter such building, structure, or premises at all reasonable times to inspect the same or to perform any duty imposed upon the building official by these construction codes, provided that if such building or premises is occupied, he shall first present proper credentials and request entry. If such building, structure, or premises is unoccupied, he shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner or other persons having charge or control of such and request entry. If entry is refused, the building official shall have recourse to every remedy provided by law to secure entry.
(2) When the building official shall have first obtained a proper inspection warrant or other remedy provided by law to secure entry, no owner or occupant or any other persons having charge, care or control of any building, structure, or premises shall fail or neglect, after proper request is made as herein provided, to promptly permit entry therein by the building official for the purpose of inspection and examination pursuant to the construction codes.
(c) Stop-work orders. Upon notice from the building official, work on any building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system that is being done contrary to the provisions of the construction codes or in a dangerous or unsafe manner, shall immediately cease. Such notice shall be in writing and shall be given to the owner of the property, or to his agent, or to the person doing the work, and shall state the conditions under which work may be resumed. Where an emergency exists, the building official shall not be required to give a written notice prior to stopping the work.
(d) Revocation of permits.
(1) Misrepresentation of application. The building official may revoke a permit or approval, issued under the provisions of the construction codes, in case there has been any false statement or misrepresentation as to the material fact in the application or plans on which the permit or approval was based.
(2) Violation of code provisions. The building official may revoke a permit upon determination by the building official that the construction erection, alteration, repair, moving, demolition, installation or replacement of the building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems for which the permit was issued is in violation of, or not in conformity with, the provisions of the construction codes.
(e) Unsafe buildings or systems. All buildings, structures, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems which are unsafe, unsanitary, or do not provide adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use, constitute a hazard to safety or health, are considered unsafe buildings or service systems.
(f) Requirements not covered by code. Any requirements necessary for the strength, stability, or proper operation of an existing or proposed building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system, or for the public safety, health, and general welfare, not specifically covered by or the construction codes, shall be determined by the building official.
(g) Alternate materials and methods. The provisions of the construction codes are not intended to prevent the use of any material or method of construction not specifically prescribed by them, provided any such alternate has been reviewed by the building official. The building official shall approve any such alternate, provided the building official finds that the alternate for the purpose intended is at least the equivalent of that prescribed in the construction codes, in quality, strength, effectiveness, fire resistance, durability, and safety. The building official shall require that sufficient evidence or proof be submitted to substantiate any claim made regarding the alternate.
